title: Variables, Outputs, Locals and Complex Types

header.html: 4c Use variables and outputs; 4d Understand and use complex types
the official Terraform Associate (004) exam content list

html:
1Input variables

Input variables make a configuration reusable: they are the parameters of a module or of the root configuration.

variable "instance_type" {
  type        = string
  description = "Size of the web server"
  default     = "t3.micro"
}

resource "aws_instance" "web" {
  ami           = "ami-0abcdef1234567890"
  instance_type = var.instance_type
}
Argument Meaning
type The allowed type (string, number, bool, list, map, object and so on)
default The value used if none is given; without a default the variable is required
description Documentation for users
sensitive Hide the value in CLI output (Module 10)
nullable Whether null is allowed
validation Custom rules (Module 9)

How values are supplied, from lowest to highest precedence:

Order Source
1 (lowest) Default in the variable block
2 Environment variables named TF_VAR_name
3 terraform.tfvars and terraform.tfvars.json
4 *.auto.tfvars and *.auto.tfvars.json (alphabetical order)
5 (highest) -var and -var-file on the command line (in the order given)

If a required variable has no value anywhere, Terraform asks for it interactively.

Exam tip

. Command-line -var and -var-file win over everything. TF_VAR_name is an environment variable. No default means the variable is required.

2Output values

Outputs expose information from a configuration: to the user after apply, or to a parent module or another configuration.

output "instance_ip" {
  value       = aws_instance.web.public_ip
  description = "Public address of the web server"
  sensitive   = false
}
Fact Detail
Shown after apply Root module outputs are printed
terraform output Reads outputs from the state; terraform output -json for scripts
sensitive = true Hides the value in output
In a child module An output is the only way the parent can read a value (Module 12)

3Local values

Locals name an expression so you can reuse it and avoid repetition. They are not inputs: callers cannot set them.

locals {
  name_prefix = "${var.project}-${var.environment}"
  common_tags = {
    Project     = var.project
    Environment = var.environment
  }
}

Reference with local.name_prefix (singular local).

Exam tip

. Variables are inputs; locals are internal names; outputs are results. The block is locals, the reference is local..

4Types and complex types

Kind Type Example
Primitive string "web"
number 3
bool true
Collection list(type) Ordered, allows duplicates: ["a", "b"]
set(type) Unordered, unique values
map(type) Keys to values of one type: { a = 1, b = 2 }
Structural tuple([...]) Ordered, each element its own type
object({...}) Named attributes with their own types
Special any Let Terraform decide the type 
variable "servers" {
  type = list(object({
    name = string
    size = string
  }))
  default = [
    { name = "web", size = "small" },
    { name = "db", size = "large" },
  ]
}
Exam tip

. List = ordered, set = unique and unordered, map = keys and values of one type, object = named attributes of different types. A type constraint makes Terraform convert or reject wrong values.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A variable block has no default value and the user supplies none. What does Terraform do on plan?

  • AAsks the user for the value
  • BUses the empty string
  • CFails without any message
  • DUses the value from the last run
Show the answer

Answer: A. A required variable with no value is requested interactively.

S2Which source of a variable value has the highest precedence?

  • AThe default in the variable block
  • BA terraform.tfvars file
  • CThe -var option on the command line
  • DAn environment variable named TF_VAR_name
Show the answer

Answer: C. Command-line -var and -var-file override all other sources.

S3How is the value of a local named name_prefix referenced?

  • Avar.name_prefix
  • Blocal.name_prefix
  • Clocals.name_prefix
  • Doutput.name_prefix
Show the answer

Answer: B. Locals are defined in a locals block and referenced with the singular prefix local.

S4Which type holds unique values with no order?

  • Alist
  • Btuple
  • Cset
  • Dmap
Show the answer

Answer: C. A set holds unique values and has no order; a list is ordered and may repeat values.

S5A child module must give its parent the ID of a network it creates. What should the module declare?

  • AA variable block with a default
  • BAn output block with the ID
  • CA local value with the ID
  • DA provider alias for the parent
Show the answer

Answer: B. Outputs are the only way a parent module can read values from a child module.

S6Which command shows the output values stored in the state?

  • Aterraform show -output
  • Bterraform console
  • Cterraform output
  • Dterraform state outputs
Show the answer

Answer: C. terraform output reads the output values from the state.

5.2 Recall questions

R1What makes an input variable required?

Show the answer

Having no default value.

R2What is the name of an environment variable for a variable called region?

Show the answer

TF_VAR_region.

R3What do outputs expose?

Show the answer

Values to the user or to a parent module.

R4What is the difference between list and set?

Show the answer

A list is ordered and may repeat; a set is unique and unordered.

R5What type has named attributes of different types?

Show the answer

object.

R6How do you reference a local value?

Show the answer

local.NAME.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Variables type, default, description, sensitive, validation; no default = required
Precedence default, TF_VAR_, tfvars, auto.tfvars, -var and -var-file (highest)
Outputs expose values; terraform output; child module outputs reach the parent
Locals named expressions; local.NAME
Types string, number, bool; list, set, map; tuple, object; any
